newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot stops London-Tokyo cargo route.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot stops London-Tokyo cargo route.

text.p: Aeroflot Russian International Airlines has suspended its regular cargo flights on the London-Tokyo-London route but plans to resume them later, a senior airline official said on Tuesday.
Deputy chief of Aeroflot cargo department Yevgeny Blinov told Reuters that the carrier would replace the Ilyushin-76T freighter on the route, because it was inefficient.
"Il-76T had a very low load factor carrying cargoes on pallets," Blinov said.
But he said Aeroflot had kept these flights in the schedule and planned to use another type of aircraft on the route.

"We plan to lease a DC-10 or Boeing 747 for it," he said, adding that it would be possible to operate the route jointly with another airline. Blinov did not say which carrier could be Aeroflot's partner.
Currently, Aeroflot cargo operates Antonov-124-100, Il-76T, Tupolev-204 and leased DC-10-30 freighters on more than 50 regular flights weekly around the world.
